# Review protocol

Match review effort to the task. For routine short work, self-check against the brief and relevant medium guidance. For substantial customer pitches, substantial articles and consequential PRDs, use a fresh reviewer when available and authorized. Honor explicit review requests and scope; a review-only assignment does not authorize modifying the source.

Give the reviewer the purpose, audience, medium, raw facts, constraints, approved examples/feedback and complete draft or relevant surface. Include the requested mode. Omit the writer's private rationale, prior scores, desired score and version identity. Do not omit user requirements to achieve blinding. Ask for diagnosis only; the reviewer should not publish or mutate the artifact.

Only the owning writer or review coordinator commissions reviewers. A delegated reviewer returns findings directly; it must not spawn another reviewer or reinvoke the writer. Share one review across cooperating writing and Sales skills when it covers both assignments.

Assess reader usefulness, argument, evidence, medium fit, voice and preservation. Require the exact problematic passage, why it matters to this brief and the smallest useful correction. Identify strong material worth retaining. Do not manufacture faults or force a numerical quota of changes. Flag missing evidence and unresolved decisions rather than filling them in.

The writer should apply supported fixes within the authorized scope and may reject suggestions that violate facts, the brief or approved wording. For a major revision—material changes to the argument, structure, tone, offer or substantial portions of the text—rerun the full applicable rubric on the complete final artifact before delivery, using a fresh independent reviewer when available and permitted. A check that requested edits were made does not replace this review. For minor corrections, recheck affected passages and consequential dependencies. Use at most two revision/review cycles by default; stop sooner when no material defects remain. If a consequential issue remains unresolved, state it or ask a targeted question rather than polishing indefinitely. Continue longer only for a concrete remaining defect or explicit request.

Report the real review scope. A fresh execution of the same model is independent of the drafting context, not an independent human preference judgment. If delegation is unavailable, disclose that the review was a self-check. Never chase a desired score or treat a high score as proof of effectiveness with customers.

## Final-version evaluation

Tie every score to the exact artifact reviewed (version or content hash), review date and scope. After a major revision, reassess purpose/audience, argument, evidence, practical usefulness, structure/medium fit, voice and preservation. Report author-voice fidelity separately from polish or confidence when writing in a person's voice; use their actual words, approved samples and explicit feedback, and disclose sparse evidence. Do not average away a material voice or factual failure into a ready-to-publish verdict. Check for losses in previously strong material as well as completion of requested changes. Do not expose prior scores or a desired score to the fresh judge.

If a full final-version review is unavailable or the cycle budget is exhausted, state what remains unreviewed rather than reusing an earlier rating or implying approval. Further major edits invalidate the prior final review; minor typo or formatting fixes need only a bounded check. Preserve review-only scope and the existing limit on revision cycles.
